name: Mirari
description: A powerful orb that Laquatus, Kirtar, Kamahl and Seton chase, finally found by Emperor Aboshan.

description_citations.text: "Turg". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari pulses in the Cabal's vault and spreads darkness over Otaria.
timeline.quote: Deep within the Cabal's vault, the Mirari pulsed like a dead sun—and its darkness radiated across Otaria.

citation.text: Cabal Coffers (Torment, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The land drinks power from the Mirari, transforming the Krosan Forest.
timeline.quote: The Mirari's magic transformed the Krosan Forest—and its inhabitants.

citation.text: Sudden Strength (Judgment, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Silvos is born of the Mirari and thrust out of his homeland, finding purpose in the pits.
timeline.quote: He was born of the Mirari, thrust out of his homeland before he was even aware.

citation.text: Silvos, Rogue Elemental (Onslaught, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The Mirari calls to the centaurs, changing all who heard it.
timeline.quote: The Mirari called to the centaurs, and all who heard it were forever changed.

citation.text: Centaur Glade (Onslaught, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Order clerics contain the Mirari's energy to delay Otaria's demise.
timeline.quote: Every day, Order clerics contain as much of the Mirari's energy as possible, hoping to delay Otaria's demise.

citation.text: Aura Extraction (Onslaught, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The Mirari's mutating effects grow out of control and centaurs and druids flee.
timeline.quote: As the Mirari's mutating effects grew out of control, centaurs and druids fled

citation.text: Vexing Beetle (Legions, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Kamahl feels the full force of the Mirari's pull once again.
timeline.quote: Once again, Kamahl felt the full force of the Mirari's pull, but he had learned much since the last time.

citation.text: Upwelling (Scourge, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The land drinks power from the Mirari.
timeline.quote: The land drank power from the Mirari as though it had thirsted forever.

citation.text: Mirari's Wake (World Championship Decks 2003, 2003), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: A false god tears magic from Dominaria and is slain by the Mirari sword.
timeline.quote: Even after a false god tore magic from Dominaria, power still radiated from the Mirari sword that slew her.

citation.text: Mirari's Wake (Pro Tour Promos, 2008), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The Mirari pulses in the Cabal's vault, its darkness radiating across Otaria.
timeline.quote: Deep within the Cabal's vault, the Mirari pulsed like a dead sun

citation.text: Cabal Coffers (Planechase, 2009), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Balthor opposes Kamahl when the Mirari drives him to take over all the tribes; Jeska is mortally wounded and Kamahl comes to his senses.
timeline.quote: Following Jeska's mortal wounding, Kamahl snapped out of the Mirari's influence

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "A New Home". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Balthor's spirit guides Kamahl to the Mirari-sword, then is struck down by it for the last time, bringing Kamahl to his senses.
timeline.quote: Balthor intervened only to be struck by the sword and killed for the last time

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "Balthor the spirit". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer unearths the Mirari at a forgotten villa outside Cabal City and presents it to the First, who enshrines it as the prize of the Cabal Pit.
timeline.quote: Chainer — ever loyal to the Cabal — presented it to The First

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: A Krosan dragon besieges Cabal City; Kamahl is crushed beneath its corpse and Kirtar seizes the glory and chooses the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kirtar selected the Mirari, which granted him visions of dominion.

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari is spirited away to Emperor Aboshan's court.
timeline.quote: the Mirari was spirited away to Mer Emperor Aboshan 's court

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Aboshan seizes the Mirari; his plan to flood Otaria ends in his death and the creation of the Aboshan Trench.
timeline.quote: His genocidal designs to flood Otaria culminated in his death

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids carries the Mirari back to Cabal City.
timeline.quote: the Mirari returned to Cabal City, carried by the trickster Braids

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer, having lost his mentor Skellum to pit combat arranged by the First, challenges the First with the Mirari and the name Calchexas.
timeline.quote: he challenged the First for leadership, wielding the Mirari

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl duels Chainer, who loses his humanity and dissolves into monsters; Kamahl burns the remains with the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kamahl, honoring his final plea, took up the Mirari and burned Chainer’s monstrous remains

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In the Pardic Mountains Kamahl organizes a brutal tournament, then nearly kills his sister Jeska, who is left in fiery torment by the Mirari; he rejects the artifact.
timeline.quote: Horrified, Kamahl finally rejected the artifact.

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl embraces the druids' teachings and drives a sword through Laquatus into Krosa's soil, ending the battle but leaking the Mirari's influence into the soil.
timeline.quote: He plunged the sword through the body of Laquatus and into the forested ground of Krosa.

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari's magic mutates Otarian aven and owl aven into larger, taloned forms.
timeline.quote: As the Mirari 's magic washed across Otaria, altering its inhabitants, many aven became taller and more muscular

citation.text: "Bird", section "Aven". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids leads Cabalists to the Mer Empire capital and makes a deal with Laquatus to find the Mirari; Aboshan finds it first and dies.
timeline.quote: she made a deal with Laquatus to find the Mirari for him

citation.text: "Braids", section "To the Mer Empire". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids pockets the Mirari, immune to its lure, and returns it to the First.
timeline.quote: she merely pocketed it and made her way back to Cabal City

citation.text: "Braids", section "To the Mer Empire". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer loses control of the Mirari's power in a pit fight against Kamahl; the city is condemned and abandoned.
timeline.quote: the ruined city was completely abandoned by the Cabal

citation.text: "Cabal City", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer discovers the Mirari in a ruined manor's basement but resists its call, deciding it is fit only for the First of the Cabal.
timeline.quote: Chainer resisted its call, deciding that such power was only fit for the First of the Cabal.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Cabalist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: At the Mirari games an Order justiciar and angels attack; infuriated, Chainer taps the dementia space of almost every caster on Otaria, unleashing carnage in Cabal City.
timeline.quote: brought all the creatures he found there into existence inside Cabal City.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl confronts and fights Chainer, melting off his artificial arm; Chainer's healing goes wrong and the Mirari overwhelms him.
timeline.quote: the Mirari’s power finally overwhelmed him, replacing Chainer’s entire body with a writhing mass of dementia creatures.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer begs Kamahl to kill him, and Kamahl does; the Mirari passes to Kamahl.
timeline.quote: while the Mirari now passed on to Kamahl.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer finds the Mirari outside Cabal City and hands it to the First, who is impressed by his loyalty.
timeline.quote: Despite the temptations of the orb, he decides to hand it to the head of the Cabal

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl tearfully witnesses Chainer's death and takes the Mirari as promised.
timeline.quote: Kamahl tearfully witnesses Chainer's death and takes the Mirari, as promised.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl thrusts the Mirari into the Krosan forest, mutating Otaria's people.
timeline.quote: the barbarian Kamahl thrust the Mirari

citation.text: "Dominaria (plane)", section "Coming of Karona". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari's mana waves mutate many Wirewood elves.
timeline.quote: When the Mirari started spreading its mana waves over the continent, many of the elves mutated

citation.text: "Elf", section "Otarian Elves". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Under the Mirari's influence Kamahl goes berserk, slaying most of his kin and dealing Jeska a horrific blow.
timeline.quote: Kamahl lost control and went berserk, slaying most of his kin and striking a horrific blow against Jeska

citation.text: "Jeska", section "Barbarian". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl keeps the Mirari safe from others and himself, keeping his promise to a dying Chainer.
timeline.quote: keeps the Mirari safe from others and himself

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus and Eesha try to obtain the Mirari while Jeska and Balthor try to separate it from Kamahl for fear of its corrupting influence.
timeline.quote: attempt to obtain the potent orb for themselves

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After politics and war, the Mirari, attached to Kamahl's sword, is implanted through Laquatus's corpse into the Krosan Forest, channeling its magic into the land.
timeline.quote: is implanted through the corpse of Laquatus and into the Krosan Forest

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: A majority of the characters are killed and the influence of the Mirari on individuals is diminished.
timeline.quote: A majority of the characters are killed

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl keeps his promise to the dying Chainer and takes the Mirari, attaching it to his sword and fighting off challengers on his way home.
timeline.quote: he takes the Mirari orb for safekeeping.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Under the Mirari's influence Kamahl unites the tribes, defeats the Elite Eight with excessive power and plunges the tribes into civil war.
timeline.quote: he proclaims himself champion; many, however, refuse his rule because he has gone mad with power, plunging the tribes into civil war.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills Laquatus with the Mirari sword, its power now bringing growth and peace, and the forest is rejuvenated.
timeline.quote: The merman dies pinned by the sword.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl wins sponsorship and enters the pits, first sees the Mirari and befriends Seton and Chainer.
timeline.quote: He first saw the Mirari when he was shown the fighters' prizes and became obsessed with obtaining them.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills a Krosan dragon attacking Cabal City but Lieutenant Kirtar is credited and takes the Mirari as his prize, starting the Battle for the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kamahl thus began his journey to claim the artifact for himself.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar uses the Mirari to crystallize much of the Order's fortress, including himself and Captain Pianna; Laquatus ends up with the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kirtar used the device to cast a devastating spell that crystallized much of the fortress

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Emperor Aboshan uses the Mirari to cause a tidal wave that devastates northern Otaria while Kamahl trains youths in Breaker Bay.
timeline.quote: Emperor Aboshan used the Mirari to cause a tidal wave that devastated the northern third of Otaria.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl is badly hurt in the Order's attack on Cabal City and wakes with snakeskin grafted by Chainer using the Mirari; he burns it off.
timeline.quote: To cleanse himself of the additions, Kamahl burnt off his skin and left the hospital

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari drives Chainer mad and warps him into a mass of dementia beasts; dying, he gives the Mirari to Kamahl, who attaches it to his sword.
timeline.quote: As Chainer died, he gave the Mirari to Kamahl

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl returns home, is dominated by the Mirari and tries to take all the tribes under his dictatorship, dividing the barbarians.
timeline.quote: Initially, he was content simply to return home covered in glory, but inevitably, the Mirari dominated his mind.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl and the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In battle Kamahl impales Jeska with the Mirari-sword, leaving an incurable wound; shocked, he resolves to be rid of the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kamahl viciously impaling Jeska with his Mirari-sword

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl and the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl strikes down Laquatus with the Mirari-sword, leaves it in the ground and forsakes the Mirari for a druidic life.
timeline.quote: With that act, Kamahl forsook the Mirari and his violent past

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl meets Karona, then resolves she must be stopped; he retrieves the Mirari from Laquatus's corpse with Balthor's ghost's help.
timeline.quote: it was only through Balthor's spiritual sacrifice that Kamahl managed to gain control over the Mirari-sword

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Karona's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn creates Argentum and sends probes to Dominaria, one of which becomes the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Karn later created Argentum , a plane of mathematical perfection.

citation.text: "Karn", section "Argentum". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn turns the Mirari into the golem Memnarch, whose contact with Karn's glistening oil leads him to transform Argentum into Mirrodin.
timeline.quote: he decided to turn Argentum into Mirrodin

citation.text: "Karn", section "Argentum". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Locked out of Mirrodin, Karn sends dreams to Glissa; after Memnarch falls he turns him back into the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Karn turned Memnarch back into the Mirari and left it in the care of Glissa, Slobad , and Geth .

citation.text: "Karn", section "Argentum". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar receives the Mirari and is overcome by the power it offers him.
timeline.quote: Kirtar was overcome by the power the device offered him

citation.text: "Kirtar", section "The Battle for the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar organizes a coup, demands command of the Order and uses the Mirari to engulf Pianna in crystals.
timeline.quote: Kirtar used the Mirari on Pianna, creating a wave of crystals that engulfed her.

citation.text: "Kirtar", section "Death". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The spell spreads out of control; Turg steals the Mirari and Kirtar fades to nothing as the spell drains his essence.
timeline.quote: Kirtar faded away to nothing as the spell drained away his very essence to feed itself.

citation.text: "Kirtar", section "Death". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn leaves Argentum to train Jeska, granting his warden the Mirari orb and stewardship of the plane.
timeline.quote: The second was stewardship over the plane itself.

citation.text: "Memnarch", section "Warden". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn restores the souls, causing the Vanishing, destroys Memnarch's body and gives the Mirari to Glissa, Slobad and Geth.
timeline.quote: Karn destroyed Memnarch's body, recovering the Mirari

citation.text: "Memnarch", section "Downfall". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer finds the Mirari in an old mansion and gives it to the First as a tournament prize.
timeline.quote: The Mirari was found by Chainer in an old mansion

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Discovery". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar claims the Mirari to destroy it but is corrupted and uses it to kill Pianna.
timeline.quote: Instead, he took it to the Order's citadel and used it to kill Pianna

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Discovery". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Aboshan pours mana into the Mirari, flooding the northern third of Otaria; the spell destroys the capital and kills him.
timeline.quote: He poured mana into the Mirari to try to make the vision a reality, creating a massive wave that flooded the northern third of Otaria.

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Discovery". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids takes the Mirari back to the Patriarch.
timeline.quote: fell into the hands of Braids

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Discovery". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl attaches the Mirari to his sword and tries to unite the Pardic barbarians by force.
timeline.quote: He attached it to the pommel of his sword and tried to use its power to unite the Pardic barbarians under his rule.

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Problems in Cabal City". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills Laquatus in Krosa and leaves the Mirari-sword in the ground.
timeline.quote: Kamahl finishing the merman by driving the Mirari-sword through Laquatus and into the ground

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari pours energy into Krosa, mutating creatures and plants across Otaria.
timeline.quote: the Mirari now began pouring energy into Krosa

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn reveals the Mirari's origins and takes it back to Argentum.
timeline.quote: Karn appeared and revealed the Mirari's humble origins and took it back to Argentum

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn reshapes the Mirari into the sentient Memnarch, protector of Argentum.
timeline.quote: Karn reshaped the Mirari as a sentient being

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Memnarch". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After Memnarch's defeat Karn melts him down, revealing the Mirari, left in the care of Glissa, Slobad and Geth.
timeline.quote: Karn returned to his plane and melted down Memnarch to his core, revealing the Mirari underneath.

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Memnarch". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl plants the Mirari in Krosa; its power soaks into the continent and mutates the inhabitants, driving forest beasts mad.
timeline.quote: it was he who planted the Mirari there thinking that without a wielder the artifact would be harmless.

citation.text: "Mutant", section "Otarian Mutants". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari's magic washes across Otaria, making many aven taller and more muscular with razor-like talons.
timeline.quote: many aven became taller and more muscular

citation.text: "Mutant", section "Otarian Mutants". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn leaves Memnarch in control of Argentum.
timeline.quote: Karn left one of his creations, Memnarch , a golem created from the Mirari , in control of the plane

citation.text: "New Phyrexia (plane)", section "Memnarch's reign". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl leaves the Pardic Mountains and his sister Jeska to make a name for himself, drawn by the Mirari.
timeline.quote: In leaving behind the Pardic Mountains, where age-old territorial skirmishes between the barbarians and dwarves continue to rage on, Kamahl leaves his sister Jeska

citation.text: "Odyssey", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: A Krosan dragon attacks; Kamahl lands the killing blow but is pinned under the carcass and Kirtar takes the glory and the sphere.
timeline.quote: Despite Kamahl being he who dealt the killing blow, he remains pinned down underneath the carcass, and Kirtar takes the glory instead.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar tries to gain control of the Order with the sphere but its power devastates the city, leaving him and Pianna dead; Turg takes the artifact.
timeline.quote: leaving him and Pianna dead, and the city in ruins.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Aboshan finds the Mirari in his treasury and unleashes its power, submerging a third of Otaria and destroying his capital.
timeline.quote: submerging a third of Otaria and destroying his capital.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus and Fulla stop Aboshan at the cost of Turg's life and take the Mirari to Cabal City.
timeline.quote: Laquatus and Fulla manage to stop him before the damage is too great, at the cost of Turg's life.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl relocates to the Krosan Forest with the Mirari and becomes a druid of Krosa.
timeline.quote: Kamahl has relocated to the Krosan Forest with the Mirari and becomes a druid of Krosa.

citation.text: "Onslaught", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari's power begins mutating the forest's residents, growing some to gigantic proportions.
timeline.quote: The power of the Mirari begins to work on the forest, mutating its residents and growing some of them to gigantic proportions.

citation.text: "Onslaught", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl has just slain Laquatus with the Mirari sword, causing vegetation to flourish around it.
timeline.quote: Kamahl has just slain Laquatus using the Mirari sword.

citation.text: "Onslaught (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: A century after the Invasion the Mirari appears, starting wars that devastate the continent.
timeline.quote: A century after the Invasion, the Mirari appeared there, initiating a series of destructive wars that devastated much of the continent.

citation.text: "Otaria", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Pianna travels to Krosa when Kirtar slaughters the forest's animals and orders him to withdraw.
timeline.quote: Pianna ordered Kirtar to withdraw his remaining men back to the citadel

citation.text: "Pianna", section "Confronting Kirtar". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Pianna maps the attacks, finds they match Kirtar's route, and asks him to destroy the Mirari; he refuses and plots a coup.
timeline.quote: He instead organized a coup against Pianna by his fellow aven warriors

citation.text: "Pianna", section "Death". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar traps Pianna in solid crystal with the Mirari, killing her; the spell destroys the citadel and Kirtar.
timeline.quote: Kirtar used the Mirari to trap Pianna in a solid crystal, instantly killing her

citation.text: "Pianna", section "Death". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari falls into Kamahl's hands, and his actions inadvertently lead to the Rebirth of Karona.
timeline.quote: saw it eventually falling into the hands of Kamahl , whose actions inadvertently led to the Rebirth of Karona

citation.text: "Rift Era", section "Rise and Fall of Karona". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Karn uses the Mirari's core to create Memnarch, protector of the artificial plane of Argentum.
timeline.quote: the planeswalker Karn used the Mirari’s core to create Memnarch

citation.text: "Rift Era", section "Creation and Corruption of Mirrodin". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl, guided by Balthor's ghost, retrieves his sword from Laquatus's corpse and defeats the giant Laquatus again.
